findings.title: The owner can lose control of moderation to an arbitrary first signup — absent ADMIN_EMAIL, the first caller of /api/me is made admin without checking their email domain
findings.observed: A fresh deployment grants the first signed-in account admin regardless of email domain.

findings.title: Reviewers can publish a previously rejected clip or reverse an approval — the moderation update does not require the clip to still be pending
findings.observed: POST approve succeeds after reject and exposes the previously rejected clip.

findings.title: Visitors lose the builder, checkout and wall when authentication is unavailable — the global Clerk wrapper withholds every route until Clerk config succeeds
findings.observed: Disabled or unreachable Clerk config leaves / blank, then shows only a sign-in error.

findings.title: Dancers still cannot apply follow-up voice edits — both changed edit attempts request the unsupported Claude model and return the original kit
findings.observed: Both edit attempts use claude-sonnet-5-5; failures return applied=false.

findings.title: Dancers can still receive a firework they explicitly removed — the changed editor derives removals from model output and misses requested items left in the cart
findings.observed: A model that keeps a requested-to-remove item can return it in the saved edited kit.

findings.title: Dancers cannot remove the only firework type in a kit — the changed editor rejects a model response with no remaining cues before padding replacements
findings.observed: Removing the only cue type yields applied=false when the model returns no cues.

findings.title: Crews lose access to all clips posted before moderation — new wall and video queries require a status that old clip rows never had, with no migration or review path
findings.observed: Pre-upgrade clips have no status and disappear from the wall, video route and review queue.

findings.title: A signed-out administrator's retained token can still review clips until it expires — protected routes verify JWT signatures but never check Clerk session revocation
findings.observed: A signed-out session's unexpired JWT still passes the local signature and expiry checks.

findings.title: An admin can grant moderation to an account outside the allowed email domains — the role endpoint promotes any member and the admin guard checks only the stored role
findings.observed: Promoting a member from any email domain grants moderation without a domain check.

findings.title: Anonymous oversized uploads can exhaust server disk and interrupt other crews — FastAPI parses the complete multipart file before the handler enforces its size limit
findings.observed: The multipart parser can spool an arbitrarily large upload before the 60 MB check runs.

findings.title: Concurrent anonymous video uploads can stall the builder and wall for other visitors — each request starts an unrestricted CPU-intensive ffmpeg transcode
findings.observed: Each anonymous video upload can start a separate ffmpeg process for up to 180 seconds.

findings.title: Dancers still get too few group wands in a budgeted fallback kit — the changed fitter trims crew wands before replacing costlier cues
findings.observed: Under a tight budget, the fitter removes extra crew wands before swapping expensive cues.

findings.title: Moderators can permanently lock the team out of the review queue — concurrent demotions check the admin count separately from the role update
findings.observed: Two concurrent demotions can both observe 2 admins and leave 0.

findings.title: A shared cache can expose an unapproved crew video after an admin previews it — the authenticated video route returns publicly cacheable bytes
findings.observed: Authenticated pending-video responses are marked public and cacheable for 86400 seconds.

findings.title: Crews can unintentionally publish under the wrong name — both upload forms and the server accept an empty crew and substitute Phnom Penh crew
findings.observed: An empty crew posts successfully as 'Phnom Penh crew' instead of a validation error.

findings.title: Crews lose footage after the first minute without warning — the upload transcoder silently truncates every source video to 60 seconds
findings.observed: A 90-second upload is stored as only its first 60 seconds and reported pending.

findings.title: Returning visitors cannot like a clip in a later week — the permanent clip/device unique key prevents a new weekly like after the old one expires
findings.observed: After seven days the count falls to 0 but the device remains liked and cannot add 1.

findings.title: The wall buries a leading crew's clips beneath lower-ranked crews — it sorts individual clip likes before computing crew totals
findings.observed: Two 6-like clips rank below a rival's 10-like clip despite their crew leading 12 to 10.

findings.title: Crews still lose approved wall posts and rankings as the wall grows — the changed list reads at most 500 and renders only 60 without pagination
findings.observed: Approved clip 61 is unreachable; clips beyond the first 500 are not ranked.

findings.title: A failed clip post still leaves a private recording stranded in storage — the changed upload stores the object before inserting Mongo and never rolls it back
findings.observed: A database insert failure leaves the uploaded MP4 in object storage without a clip row.

findings.title: Crews can still submit duplicate clips after an interrupted upload — the changed server generates a new ID on every retry without an idempotency key
findings.observed: Retrying after a lost response creates a second pending clip.

findings.title: Rejected crew videos can remain playable from browser caches for a day — the changed serving helper marks both public and admin responses publicly cacheable
findings.observed: Video responses include Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400 after moderation changes.

findings.title: Visitors see stale weekly standings after liking a clip — the optimistic handler ignores the server count and never recomputes or reloads the ranking
findings.observed: Liking a clip changes its number but leaves the top-crew strip and order stale.

findings.title: Reviewers can miss pending submissions when loading fails — the queue converts all request errors into the empty state
findings.observed: A failed queue request displays 'Nothing to review' instead of an error.

findings.title: Reviewers cannot inspect a submission or tell why it failed — a failed authenticated video fetch is swallowed and the loading spinner never ends
findings.observed: A failed pending-video fetch leaves the reviewer with an endless spinner.

findings.title: Phone viewers can wait for the whole video before playback or seeking starts — range handling fetches the complete storage object before slicing it
findings.observed: A cold byte-range request downloads the entire storage object before returning its slice.

findings.title: Live and preview role management can use the wrong environment — wall.py computes ENV before server.py loads the configured Clerk key
findings.observed: A live Clerk key supplied only in .env still makes ENV equal 'preview'.

findings.title: Dancers can hear the beat ahead of a still-loading preview — Resume starts audio without checking whether the 3D stage is ready
findings.observed: Pause then resume during loading starts the beat while the preview still reads 0:00.

findings.title: Older submissions cannot be reviewed when the queue exceeds 200 clips — the server silently caps the pending list and the admin UI has no pagination
findings.observed: Pending clip 201 is omitted from the review queue with no next-page control.

findings.title: Visitors can inflate a crew's weekly ranking with repeated likes — the public like endpoint trusts an arbitrary caller-supplied device identifier
findings.observed: Changing the client-supplied device_id counts another like on the same clip.

findings.title: Wall loads slow as likes accumulate — each visit scans clip_likes for device_id because the unique index begins with clip_id
findings.observed: The wall's device_id lookup lacks a device_id-first index.

findings.title: Moderation gets slower as clips accumulate — the review query must sort matching clips without an index on status, is_deleted and created_at
findings.observed: The pending queue's status/is_deleted/created_at sort lacks a matching compound index.

findings.title: Khmer-speaking reviewers cannot use the sign-in and moderation screens in their selected language — the new Clerk and admin controls bypass the language dictionary
findings.observed: The sign-in and review controls and access errors remain English in Khmer mode.

findings.title: Clients cannot change roles through the specified admin endpoint — the backend and UI instead use /api/users/{id}/role
findings.observed: PATCH /api/admin/users/{id}/role has no matching backend route.

findings.title: API consumers cannot reliably identify and preview clips using the documented contract — clip responses omit crew_name and review video references
findings.observed: Clip responses expose crew, not crew_name, and the admin list supplies no video URL.

findings.title: Dancers can still get a removed firework after excluding every catalog item — the changed fitter falls back to item 6 even when it is banned
findings.observed: With all 12 catalog IDs removed, the filler falls back to banned item 6.

findings.title: Dancers can still have removed fireworks return during a different add request — the changed editor trusts every model-reported addition whenever any add word appears
findings.observed: An unrelated model-reported added ID is unbanned whenever the command contains 'add'.

findings.title: Dancers still lose their chosen drop firework under a tight budget — the changed budget fitter substitutes the protected drop
findings.observed: When necessary to meet budget, the fitter swaps out the selected drop cue.

findings.title: Dancers still receive their largest firework away from the beat drop — the changed planner keeps a cheaper existing drop cue without comparing the other cues
findings.observed: A cheaper existing drop cue remains even when another cue is more expensive.

findings.title: Dancers using the 2D fallback still cannot freeze the drop flash and shake — the changed preview keeps the fallback animation running while paused
findings.observed: On the 2D fallback, flash and shake decay and change while the clock is paused.

findings.title: Dancers on tall narrow phones still see a stretched preview — the changed phone frame clamps width independently of height
findings.observed: Phone frame width is capped independently of its height on tall narrow screens.

findings.title: Dancers still see DROP stuck on the final frame for late drops — the changed label expires against a clock capped at 15 seconds
findings.observed: A drop at 14–15 seconds remains displayed at the final 15-second frame.

findings.title: Keyboard users can still activate hidden kit controls behind the preview — the changed overlay has no focus management or dialog semantics
findings.observed: The fullscreen preview has no dialog semantics or focus trap.

findings.title: Dancers can still see a mixed preview when the kit changes — the changed preview receives live cues while its director retains the old fired-cue state
findings.observed: A replacement kit changes preview cues without resetting the director's fired-cue set.

findings.title: Dancers who cannot record can still leave a compositor running — the changed recording failure handler does not cancel its animation loop or stop its stream
findings.observed: A recorder setup exception leaves the compositor animation loop and stream active.

findings.title: Dancers can still post or download a broken recording as successful — the changed recorder saves and offers every onstop blob even after an error
findings.observed: A recorder error can be followed by onstop saving a partial blob and showing success.

findings.title: Crews can still post a clip under the wrong kit and song — the changed preview saves only the blob and the post panel uses the live kit prop
findings.observed: The recording stores no kit ID; the post panel uses the current live kit prop.

findings.title: Other allowed Gmail and Yahoo reviewers cannot approve clips by default — the configured fallback makes only the first account admin instead of applying the requested domain rule
findings.observed: A second new Gmail or Yahoo account is assigned member when an admin already exists.

findings.title: Admins cannot reliably select the right person to grant or remove moderation access — the user list exposes no name or email, only provider IDs
findings.observed: The Users panel identifies accounts only by opaque Clerk user IDs.

findings.title: Visitors are not told that their like was not saved — the like handler catches errors and silently reloads instead of reporting failure
findings.observed: A failed like silently reloads the wall without a failure message.

findings.title: Liking a clip slows as weekly activity grows — each like aggregates every recent like across the entire wall instead of counting the selected clip
findings.observed: Every like recomputes counts for all clips liked during the last seven days.

findings.title: Crews still cannot post or play videos on deployments configured with a storage proxy only in .env — storage resolves its host before dotenv is loaded
findings.observed: A storage proxy defined only in .env is ignored because STORAGE_BASE is set before dotenv loads.

findings.title: Admins can mistake a temporary connection failure for lost permissions — the review page maps every /api/me error to the no-access screen
findings.observed: A failed /api/me request displays 'Your account doesn't have admin access.'

findings.title: Admins cannot tell why the user-management list is empty when loading fails — the panel silently discards its request error
findings.observed: A failed users request leaves a blank Users panel without an error or retry.

findings.title: Dancers can still lose unrelated fireworks from later edits — the changed editor treats all model-omitted cart items as explicitly removed
findings.observed: A combined remove/budget edit bans every old cart item omitted by the model.

findings.title: Dancers can still lose their stored delivery on an unrelated voice edit — the changed editor trusts model delivery fields even when the command did not request a change
findings.observed: A model's unsolicited delivery spot or time overwrites the stored delivery on another edit.

findings.title: Dancers can still receive an over-budget kit after a riel voice edit — the changed editor trusts a positive model budget over the currency parser
findings.observed: A positive model budget overrides the parser's value for a riel command.

findings.title: Dancers still cannot lower a voice-edited budget to zero — the changed editor treats parsed zero as absent
findings.observed: A parsed zero-dollar edit falls back to the previous budget.

findings.title: Dancers can still have an unrecognized voice command silently rewrite their kit — the changed editor does not validate the requested change before saving
findings.observed: A parseable model response is saved as applied even for an unrecognized command.

findings.title: Dancers can still leave orphaned kit revisions after a failed edit — the changed endpoint inserts the revision before validating its changes field
findings.observed: An invalid changes field can trigger retry after the edited kit was already inserted.

findings_minor.title: Wall visitors still cannot tell when a crew's clip was posted — the changed tile does not render created_at
findings_minor.observed: Wall tiles show crew, likes, kit and song but no posted time.

findings_minor.title: Crews cannot track progress during a long phone-video upload — the new upload never reads transfer progress
findings_minor.observed: A large upload shows only 'Uploading…', with no bytes or percentage progress.

findings_minor.title: Visitors following a mistyped link see a blank screen — the new router defines no not-found route
findings_minor.observed: An unknown path matches no Route and renders no page.

findings_minor.title: Signed-out reviewers must navigate back to Admin after logging in — the redirect drops the requested destination and uses the home fallback
findings_minor.observed: Sign-in after /admin redirects to / rather than returning to the review queue.
